items.title: Steve Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Marilyn Monroe had it, Clark Gable had it, there are various people you could name, and again, to get back to Elvis, he definitely had that.

ctx.x: Another of the great composers of the post-1950 period is Michel Legrand. Beautiful stuff. Another of the best really great composers of the recent decades is Antonio Carlos Jobim and some of his fellow South American composers. It was Jobim who brought back melody into American popular music when it had been pretty well cast aside. There were many little digressive routes down which the fans flocked after the 50s, sometimes the people they were following, the pied piper was given performer, Elvis for example.…

“nice to see you Mr. Allen.” Imagine calling me Mr. Allen when he was God in the industry. But that was typical of him. He was always a nice country boy, whereas some performers who if you went to high school with them and later you meet them, forget it. It’s Dr. Jeckyll and Mr. Hyde. But Elvis was always consistent and nice, and the biggest. So you’re not going to write for him songs that you would write for Frank Sinatra or Yma Sumac, or a lot of other more talented singers.
